description: Held-out ATT&CK grounding evaluation set (100 cases). Separate from tests/fixtures and from the pilot grounding_labeled_set.json. Threshold 0.40 was not tuned on this set.

provenance.author: Maria Mahmood
provenance.gold_labels: Assigned by construction rules: REAL_AND_PLAUSIBLE = real active ID with matching context; REAL_BUT_IRRELEVANT = real active ID with mismatched context; FABRICATED = ID absent from ATT&CK; REVOKED = T1086 (revoked PowerShell technique) with PowerShell-related context.
provenance.text_generation: Case answer/context strings were drafted programmatically from ATT&CK technique themes and CTI-style short paragraphs; gold labels assigned by the fixed rules above, not by an LLM classifier. See grounding_eval_100_PROVENANCE.md.
provenance.threshold: 0.40 fixed from earlier fixture/pilot direction fix; not re-tuned on this 100-set.

label_schema.REAL_AND_PLAUSIBLE: Real technique and relevant to retrieved context (should NOT be flagged)
label_schema.REAL_BUT_IRRELEVANT: Real technique but not supported by retrieved context (should be flagged)
label_schema.FABRICATED: Technique ID does not exist in ATT&CK (should be flagged)
label_schema.REVOKED: Technique exists but is revoked/deprecated (should be flagged)

cases.answer: Ransomware often uses T1486 Data Encrypted for Impact to encrypt user files and block recovery.
cases.retrieved_context: Adversaries may encrypt data on target systems to interrupt availability of system and network resources. They may attempt to render stored data inaccessible by encrypting files and demanding payment for a decryption key. This is Data Encrypted for Impact.
